藏品名称_EN: Five-ear jar with tricolor overglaze and arabesque motifs in southern China
藏品名称_ZN: 華南三彩唐花唐草文五耳壷
描述_EN: Bright green color glaze is a special feature of this product.、Flowering on the carcass、Construct the pattern with the lotus function at the waist.。The work of this hand is called South China Three Colors.、Since the Edo period、Tea Ceremony and Valuing It。South China Three Colors、A general term for lead-glazed earthenware made in southern China.。Ancient Turkey and Northern Bertram's Crossroads（Kouachi）On the production area and the examination of the products.、Crossed-toe Three-color and Mo Hubarelu。From the 16th to the 17th Century、Wide circulation in East Asia、China and Japan Dakoku、Unearthed Ruins of Southeast Asia。
描述_ZN: The bright green glaze is characteristic of this type, and the design is composed of floral arabesques on the body and lotus petals on the hips. This type of work is called Huanan sansai, and has been highly prized as a tea jar since the Edo period. Huanan sancai is the general term for lead-glazed ceramics made in southern China. It is also called koji sansai because it was thought to have originated in Kochi in northern Vietnam in ancient times. It was widely distributed in East Asia from the 16th to 17th centuries, and has been excavated from ruins in Southeast Asia as well as China and Japan.
